## Summary

- Nine Orbit actions join the six on GitLab.com at Premium and Ultimate (#1209, #1586, #1587): `orbit.query_templates`, `orbit.response_format` and `orbit.command_list` read the query templates, the shape of a query's answer and the commands of the Orbit MCP endpoint, with the action of this server that runs each; `orbit.skill_list`, `orbit.skill_get` and `orbit.skill_file` read the skills GitLab.com deploys; `orbit.named_query` runs GitLab's named queries, whose parameters the description of its `parameters` lists; `orbit.context` resolves one reference to the summary of a work item, merge request, job, pipeline, branch or commit and, with `expand`, the graph neighborhood of the first three; and `orbit.grep` searches a group or project and returns the token and id each hit carries. A query GitLab refuses because the user has chosen no group for Orbit billing now says so, where the group is chosen and the groups to choose from. GitLab.com stopped serving Orbit to the fixture namespace on 29 October 2026, so they are built from the answers captured that morning and not yet in the Orbit record.

## Breaking changes

- The aliases `orbit.search`, `kg.search` and `knowledge_graph.search` resolve to `orbit.grep`, the search, where they resolved to `orbit.query`, which runs a graph query and takes a `query` statement rather than a `search` (#1586).

## Upgrading

1. A client or script that runs a GQL statement through `orbit.search`, `kg.search` or `knowledge_graph.search` calls `orbit.query` by its own ID; the aliases now take `orbit.grep`'s `search` and target.

## Security

None.
